source_excerpts.text:
## I moved the investigation from sensing precision to preserving a useful quantum interaction

The capability I chose is **a deterministic entangling gate through a warm, continuously noisy mediator**, acting correctly on unknown quantum inputs and preserving their correlations with an external reference.

The strongest result of this continuation is a **theory of when environmental observation preserves that interaction**. It includes an exact quantum measurement channel, a sharp thermal cost bound, an explicit observer construction, and an optimization that keeps the required gate fixed.

The central finding is consequential:

> In the architecture analysed here, estimating thermal motion through a separate cold output can remove the response that produces the entangling gate. Preserving a nonzero interaction leaves a thermal cost that better estimation alone cannot eliminate.

I preserved the returning-error sensor, finite meter, complete estimator and useful failures unchanged. The new archive includes that earlier archive alongside the new proofs, executable constructions, comparisons and results:

[:chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_140f4c3dc0b881918cb4b89c6b807b10&account_id=personal)

This is a conditional theoretical result with separate analytical and executable checks. Historical priority and a practical hardware advantage remain unestablished.

## 1. The comparison changed the question before implementation

The two-rate conventional sensor already earns quadratic information. I therefore tested whether the returning-error machinery could support a stronger capability: coherent interaction with an unknown quantum system.

Replace the classical frequency by an unknown target operator \(B\):

\[
H=Z_S\otimes B.
\]

A returned error trajectory cancels the static unknown noise axis, but its output is

\[
U=\exp[-iA(T)Z_S\otimes B],
\qquad
A(T)=\int_0^T(-1)^{N(t)}\,dt.
\]

The random signed exposure \(A(T)\) now matters as a quantum operation.

There is a genuine success with an exact event record: stopping when \(A(t)\) first reaches a chosen positive value \(a\) gives precisely \(e^{-iaZ_S\otimes B}\). The crossing occurs in even error parity. But this requires resolved timing and a physical way to stop the interaction or hand off the state.

Finite observation exposes the failure. Even perfect parity
